consensus_summary: The fatherless/orphan is the paradigmatic socially vulnerable and defenseless person lacking a human protector/provider, grouped with widows and sojourners as a stock triad under God's special guardianship; just treatment of them is the test of covenant faithfulness and pure religion, with God as 'Father of the fatherless'.
book_summary: The fatherless/orphan symbolizes God's covenant people left without their Father, identified as the remnant.
consensus_core_identification: the socially vulnerable/defenseless person (paradigmatically the literal orphan) under divine protective care
book_core_identification: God's covenant people (the remnant) left without their Father
boundary_disagreement: Consensus primary (and most alternatives) covers literal orphans plus all marginalized individuals (and secondarily spiritual orphans or national desolation); the book restricts the identification to the remnant of the covenant people in abandonment.
material_contradiction: None; the remnant is a corporate instance of the fatherless category already recognized in minority alternatives.
rationale: Minimum cores share the category of those left without paternal protection/abandonment under God, so the central referent is preserved rather than replaced. The book materially narrows extension and precision to the remnant of God's people (aligning with the minority corporate-national alternative that cites Lam 5:3 for Israel/Zion under judgment/exile), excluding the dominant individual social-vulnerable cases that form the consensus primary. This is boundary disagreement, not core contradiction or absence from the listed alternatives.
strongest_objection: Dominant biblical usage and the consensus primary treat the term as the literal-ethical category of the socially vulnerable (with God as their defender), so elevating the context-specific corporate self-description of Lam 5:3 to the definitional core over-privileges a minority application.
